men-only-hotels.title: Men-Only Hotels Blackpool: Where to Stay | Blackpool.gay
men-only-hotels.description: Planning a men only hotel Blackpool stay? Compare the men-only hotels and guest houses by the Rainbow Quarter, with walking times, house rules and booking tips.
men-only-hotels.h1: Men-only hotels and guest houses in Blackpool
men-only-hotels.intro: Three Blackpool stays are men-only, all within a few minutes of the gay bars; here is how they differ and who each one suits.
men-only-hotels.body_html:
If you are searching for a men only hotel Blackpool has a small, well-established choice. All of the options below sit on or just off Lord Street, so you step outside and you are in the Rainbow Quarter. Each one has its own house rules, so read the notes before you commit.

Which Blackpool hotels are men-only?

Three stays in our listings are men-only and adults-only:

  • The Prince Albert Hotel on Yates Street: a discreet hotel with no street signage and themed weekends. Our research lists seven en-suite rooms across three floors, reached by stairs only. Walk to Blackpool North station: about 5 minutes.
  • Trades Hotel and Bar on Lord Street: a members' hotel and late bar in joined townhouses, with the bar open daily 11am to 3am on the listed hours. Walk to the station: about 3 minutes; to Mardi Gras: about 1 minute.
  • Welhorny's on Banks Street: a private members' naturist guest house with a bar, themed weekends and bear-friendly nights. Walk to the station: about 3 minutes; to Funny Girls: about 2 minutes.

How do they compare?

StayFeelBest for
The Prince Albert HotelQuiet, discreet, smallA calm base with a lounge bar and breakfast
Trades Hotel and BarBig, sociable, late-running barStaying right where the nights end
Welhorny'sMembers' rules, naturistGuests who know the naturist and bear scene

What does men-only actually mean here?

It means men only and 18 or over, and at Trades and Welhorny's you are asked to follow members' arrangements for your stay. Do not turn up expecting to bring a guest of another gender, and read the policy when you book. Our research notes that Trades has seen a recent licence transfer and change of supervisor, so ask the hotel directly about current management and facilities. At the Prince Albert, reception hours were described inconsistently in listings, so confirm check-in arrangements before you travel.

Is a men-only hotel right for me?

Choose one if you want a stay with no mixed-group noise, a bar downstairs that suits your crowd, and the scene on your doorstep. If you would rather share the trip with friends of every gender, look at our adults-only guest houses instead; most of them welcome everyone over 18.

Planning around your stay

  • Add a late night: Man Bar and Growlr Club has a men-only cruise club upstairs, entered by wristband from the bar.
  • Show night: Funny Girls is a two to five minute stroll from all three stays.
  • Access: all three have stairs, and none lists a lift, so mention mobility needs when you book.

When should I book?

Book early for Pride and the Illuminations; see our Pride weekend hotel guide and the 48-hour weekend plan. For full venue background, the Rainbow Quarter reference site goes deeper.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

adults-only-guest-houses.title: Adults-Only Gay Guest Houses Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
adults-only-guest-houses.description: Browse adults only hotels in Blackpool that welcome LGBTQ+ guests: guest houses, bars with rooms and boutique suites, with walking times to the Rainbow Quarter.
adults-only-guest-houses.h1: Adults-only gay guest houses in Blackpool
adults-only-guest-houses.intro: Looking for an adults only hotel Blackpool gay visitors recommend? These guest houses and bars with rooms are all 18+, with walking times from each.
adults-only-guest-houses.body_html:
An adults-only stay means no children's noise at breakfast and a quieter landing after a big night. Blackpool's gay guest houses cluster around Lord Street, Cocker Street and Dickson Road, so most are a short stroll from the bars. Here is the full list, grouped by style.

Which are the adults-only guest houses?

LGBTQ+ guest houses

  • Westfield House: small, quiet, Edwardian, four-star rated, with discounted parking vouchers and non-smoking rooms. About 6 minutes to the station.
  • Lawrence House: four-star, for LGBTQ+ guests and friends, with evening meals and a roof terrace listed. Check-in 2pm to 10pm; about 4 minutes to The Flying Handbag.
  • Chaps Hotel: a long-standing LGBTQ+ hotel on Cocker Street with themed rooms, breakfast and a bar. About 5 minutes to the station.
  • Q Accommodation: boutique, room-only, seven suites, booked through Mardi Gras. About 2 minutes to the station.

Adults-only B&Bs with a bar

  • The Dragonfly: B&B-style with its own bar on Lord Street. It changed hands recently, so confirm what is included.
  • The Belvedere: a Victorian guest house on Dickson Road, long popular with LGBTQ+ visitors. It is reported to be up for sale, so check it is trading.
  • Evanescent Bar and Rooms: a laid-back bar with budget rooms on Cocker Street.
  • McGraths Bar and Hotel: 18+ rooms above a lively drag bar, with guests praising hosts, cleanliness and breakfast.

Modern and bar-led

  • Hotel Neon: a modern hotel next to a cocktail bar with a garden, on Yates Street.
  • Peek-a-Booze: budget rooms above a cabaret bar on Dickson Road.

Are all gay guest houses in Blackpool adults-only?

No. Pride Lodge on High Street and De-Lovely Hotel on Lord Street are LGBTQ+ guest houses where we have not recorded an adults-only rule, so ask when booking if that matters. Mardi Gras and Rendezvous also have rooms without a recorded age policy in our data.

Which one is quietest?

Westfield House and Lawrence House are the calmer picks: one lists a quiet tag and the other sits on a quiet street near the quarter. Anywhere above a bar, such as McGraths or Peek-a-Booze, is the opposite: ideal if you want to fall into bed after the last song.

Booking notes

  • Stairs: several listings state upper floors by stairs only, with no lift.
  • Parking: Lawrence House has no on-site parking, and nearby car parks are the answer.
  • Groups: Westfield House does not take stag or hen bookings; see our group planning guide.

Prefer men-only? See men-only hotels. Or browse every option on the main stays page.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

gay-owned-guest-houses.title: Gay-Owned & LGBTQ+ Run B&Bs Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
gay-owned-guest-houses.description: Where to find gay guest houses in Blackpool run for and by the community: what our records say about LGBTQ+ guest houses, and how to confirm ownership before you book.
gay-owned-guest-houses.h1: Gay-owned and LGBTQ+-run B&Bs in Blackpool
gay-owned-guest-houses.intro: Our records describe several guest houses as LGBTQ+ stays; here is what is confirmed, what is not, and how to ask before you book.
gay-owned-guest-houses.body_html:
Plenty of visitors want their money to stay in the community, so "gay-owned" is a fair thing to search for. We want to be straight with you: our data records which stays are LGBTQ+ guest houses, but it does not record who owns them. So we will not label any property gay-owned. What we can do is list the guest houses that describe themselves as LGBTQ+ and show you how to ask.

Which guest houses describe themselves as LGBTQ+?

  • Pride Lodge: an LGBTQ+ guest house on High Street, opposite Blackpool North station, listed with a private sauna, gym and seasonal hot tub. Reception is staffed 10am to 7pm Monday to Saturday and 11am to 5pm Sunday, with WhatsApp out of hours.
  • De-Lovely Hotel: an LGBTQ+ guest house on Lord Street with themed rooms, a well-reviewed breakfast and a cocktail bar open to non-residents.
  • Westfield House: LGBTQ+, adults-only, four-star rated, on Lord Street.
  • Lawrence House: for LGBTQ+ guests and their friends, with evening meals and a roof terrace listed.
  • Chaps Hotel: an LGBTQ+ hotel on Cocker Street with a bar and themed rooms.

Are these places gay-owned?

We cannot say. Being an LGBTQ+ guest house tells you about the welcome and the clientele, not the ownership structure. Some properties also belong to the BAGS Blackpool hoteliers group, which vets its members as LGBTQ+-friendly stays; membership is a friendliness marker, again not an ownership one.

How can I check who runs a place?

  1. Look at the property's own site or social pages; many hosts introduce themselves.
  2. Ask at booking: most guest houses are happy to explain who you will meet at reception.
  3. Read recent guest reviews, which often mention the hosts by name.

McGraths is a good example: guests rate it for its hosts, cleanliness and breakfast, which tells you about the welcome even if it does not tell you about ownership. See McGraths Bar and Hotel.

What if I want a bar and rooms in one place?

Take a look at stays above the bar, where the rooms sit over a community pub or cabaret bar.

Making a good choice

  • Want quiet: Westfield House or Lawrence House.
  • Want sauna facilities on site: Pride Lodge, as listed.
  • Want breakfast and cocktails under one roof: De-Lovely.

For all adult-only choices read adults-only gay guest houses. The Rainbow Quarter reference site also covers community businesses in more depth.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

hotels-with-a-bar.title: Stay Above the Bar: Gay Bars With Rooms Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
hotels-with-a-bar.description: Want to sleep where the party is? Gay bars with rooms in Blackpool: Peek-a-Booze, Mardi Gras, Trades, Neon and Lu-Lu's, with walking times and what to expect.
hotels-with-a-bar.h1: Stay above the bar: gay pubs with rooms in Blackpool
hotels-with-a-bar.intro: Sleep upstairs from the music at one of several Rainbow Quarter bars with rooms; here is what each offers and how to choose.
hotels-with-a-bar.body_html:
The simplest way to do a Blackpool gay weekend is to book a room in the bar. No taxis, no late walk, and the stairs are the last obstacle of the night. Several Rainbow Quarter venues run rooms, and each has a different mood.

Which bars have rooms?

  • Peek-a-Booze (72-74 Dickson Road): budget adults-only rooms above a cabaret bar. Food daily 9am to 7pm on listed hours. About 3 minutes to Funny Girls.
  • Mardi Gras (41-43 Lord Street): a three-area pub with cabaret, karaoke and Sunday roasts. About 3 minutes to the station.
  • Trades Hotel and Bar (51-55 Lord Street): men-only, with a bar listed open daily 11am to 3am. Men only and 18+.
  • Hotel Neon (15 Yates Street): an adults-only hotel with a cocktail bar and a garden, usually open Thursday to Sunday.
  • Lu-Lu's Cabaret Lounge (78b-82 Dickson Road): about 26 en-suite rooms and two bars side by side. Bring cash. About 4 minutes to Funny Girls.
  • Rendezvous Bar and Rooms (15-17 Lord Street): a small bar with rooms at the station end of Lord Street, closing around 10pm.
  • McGraths Bar and Hotel, Evanescent Bar and Rooms and The Dame Lane: further bars with rooms, with drag, karaoke or bingo.

How noisy are rooms above a bar?

Expect music on show nights. Peek-a-Booze runs bingo and karaoke through the week, Lu-Lu's has cabaret Friday to Sunday from 7pm, and Mardi Gras is listed until 3am at the weekend. If you want sleep, ask for a room away from the bar or choose Rendezvous, which closes early. If you want to be part of it, stay at Mardi Gras or Peek-a-Booze.

Can I bundle a room with a show?

Peek-a-Booze suggests asking about room-and-show deals if you are staying for Funny Girls just up the road; Funny Girls is about 3 minutes away on foot. Ask any property what packages exist before you pay.

What about stairs and accessibility?

Most of these properties have upper floors reached by stairs only; Peek-a-Booze and Mardi Gras both state no lift, and Lu-Lu's has steps at the entrance. Phone ahead if you have mobility needs.

Which should I choose?

  • Lively and cheap: Peek-a-Booze or Lu-Lu's.
  • Community pub with food: Mardi Gras.
  • Quiet cocktails and rooms: Hotel Neon.
  • Men-only: Trades.

Prefer a guest house with no bar? See adults-only gay guest houses, or check the hotels near Queen Street.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

near-queen-street.title: Hotels Near Queen Street Blackpool: Walk Times | Blackpool.gay
near-queen-street.description: Hotels near Queen Street Blackpool with real walking times to The Flying Handbag: gay guest houses, bars with rooms and adults-only stays ranked by distance.
near-queen-street.h1: Gay-friendly hotels a short walk from Queen Street
near-queen-street.intro: Queen Street is the late-night strip; these stays are the closest, with walking times to The Flying Handbag, the strip’s flagship bar.
near-queen-street.body_html:
Queen Street is where Blackpool's late nights land. If you want to roll home in minutes, pick a stay close to The Flying Handbag at number 44. The times below are walking minutes from each stay to that bar.

Which stays are closest to Queen Street?

StayWalk to The Flying HandbagType
Pride Lodge1 minuteLGBTQ+ guest house
Rendezvous Bar and Rooms1 minuteBar with rooms
Q Accommodation2 minutesAdults-only suites
Mardi Gras2 minutesPub with rooms
Welhorny's3 minutesMen-only
The Blackpool North3 minutesPublic bar with rooms
Lawrence House4 minutesAdults-only guest house
Trades Hotel and Bar4 minutesMen-only
Peek-a-Booze4 minutesRooms above a cabaret bar
Evanescent Bar and Rooms4 minutesBar with rooms

What is on Queen Street itself?

The Flying Handbag is the purpose-built flagship, with a sun terrace, food and karaoke, and its listed events include Monday Mayhem from 8pm until 3am, QuizMania on Wednesdays, Thirsty Thursday and a Friday night with Miss Amber. Check current times before you go; see our nightlife guide for other bars.

Is there a good stay for quiet sleepers near the strip?

Lawrence House is on a quiet street, four minutes from the strip, with evening meals and a roof terrace. Q Accommodation is two minutes away and room-only, so you will want breakfast elsewhere.

Do I need to stay close?

Not necessarily. Everything in the quarter is compact: even The Dame Lane, the furthest listed stay, is 8 minutes from The Flying Handbag. Choose by mood and budget first, and distance second.

Tips

  • Funny Girls is 1 to 3 minutes from the nearest stays for an early show, then walk to Queen Street.
  • Look at stays near Blackpool North station if you arrive by train.
  • Taxis wait outside Funny Girls and at the station.

More reference detail on Queen Street is available on Rainbow Quarter reference site.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

near-blackpool-north-station.title: Hotels Near Blackpool North Station | Blackpool.gay
near-blackpool-north-station.description: Hotels near Blackpool North station for an LGBTQ+ weekend: gay guest houses and bars with rooms ranked by walking minutes, so you can arrive by train and be inside quickly.
near-blackpool-north-station.h1: Gay-friendly stays near Blackpool North station
near-blackpool-north-station.intro: Arriving by train? These LGBTQ+ stays are the shortest walks from Blackpool North, with minutes from the platform exit to each door.
near-blackpool-north-station.body_html:
Blackpool North is the town's main station and sits on the edge of the Rainbow Quarter. If you are travelling light, you can be at your guest house within minutes. Here are the stays, with walking times worked out from the owner's coordinates.

Which stays are nearest to the station?

StayWalk from station

Rendezvous Bar and Rooms2 minutes
Q Accommodation2 minutes

Peek-a-Booze5 minutes

Which is the best arrival stay?

For a first-time visitor, Pride Lodge is hard to beat on distance: one minute from the station, with listed reception hours of 10am to 7pm Monday to Saturday and 11am to 5pm Sunday. If you arrive later, they list WhatsApp out of hours. The Blackpool North is a handy first stop with a public bar open from midday.

What can I drop into right away?

  • Garlands on Talbot Road: free entry, and resident queens from mid-afternoon on the listed times.
  • Funny Girls: about two minutes from the station.
  • The Flying Handbag: noon opening on the listed hours.

What if I am arriving by car instead?

You do not need a station-side stay. Pride Lodge sells parking passes at reception that you must buy before parking; Westfield House offers discounted parking vouchers; Lawrence House has no on-site parking. Read our getting there and getting home guide for all options.

Are the walks step-free?

We have no step-by-step accessibility data for the routes, and several of the stays have stairs. Check the individual stay page, and see our Queen Street stays for the next ring out.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

budget-stays.title: Cheap Gay Hotels & B&Bs in Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
budget-stays.description: Budget gay friendly hotels Blackpool visitors can book: simple B&Bs and rooms above bars, plus the one published price and how to keep costs down.
budget-stays.h1: Budget stays for a gay weekend in Blackpool
budget-stays.intro: You can stay in the Rainbow Quarter without a big bill: these simpler stays and bar rooms suit tighter budgets, with the one listed price.
budget-stays.body_html:
Blackpool is already one of the better-value places for an LGBTQ+ weekend, and the quarter has a handful of simpler stays. We only quote one price because it is the only one published in our data: rooms at Lawrence House from about £50 with breakfast. For everything else, treat the descriptions as guides and check rates directly.

Which stays are described as budget or simple?

  • The B&B Blackpool: a simple, budget B&B with a small bar on Cocker Street. Pre-book the £5 parking if driving; the two attic singles have limited headroom.
  • Peek-a-Booze: budget adults-only rooms above a cabaret bar on Dickson Road.
  • Lu-Lu's Cabaret Lounge: a budget LGBTQ+ cabaret bar with about 26 en-suite rooms. Cash only for the bar.
  • Evanescent Bar and Rooms: budget adults-only rooms above a laid-back bar.
  • Trades Hotel and Bar: a large men-only hotel with free breakfast listed in our research; reviews are mixed, with the bar praised and some guests reporting room condition issues.
  • Lawrence House: about £50 with breakfast, four-star, adults-only.

How do I keep the cost down?

  1. Go midweek or in spring and winter, the cheapest periods in our season notes. See quiet midweek breaks.
  2. Pick a stay close to the bars so you skip taxis; most are 1 to 6 minutes from the station.
  3. Choose a free night: Garlands has free entry and daily drag.
  4. Ask Peek-a-Booze about room-and-show deals if you are seeing Funny Girls.

What is cheap to do while you are here?

Free bingo runs on Wednesday evenings at Peek-a-Booze, with Play Your Cards Right at 9pm, and Garlands lists free entry every day from mid-afternoon. Funny Girls has standing tickets from about £10, with seats about £17 to £35 depending on the night; see planning a drag night.

Are budget stays safe and welcoming?

They are LGBTQ+ venues, so the welcome is a given, but simple means simple. Several have stairs only, and some rooms have limited headroom or a steep staircase. Read each stay's page, and our safety page for late-night tips.

When is the best time to book?

Pride weekend and Illuminations weekends fill first and rooms cost most; check Pride weekend hotels. Everything else is a better bet for bargains.

pride-weekend-hotels.title: Blackpool Pride Weekend Hotels: Where to Stay | Blackpool.gay
pride-weekend-hotels.description: Where to stay for Blackpool Pride: hotels, guest houses and bars with rooms close to the parade and Rainbow Quarter street party, plus when to book.
pride-weekend-hotels.h1: Where to stay for Blackpool Pride weekend
pride-weekend-hotels.intro: Pride is the busiest weekend of the LGBTQ+ year in Blackpool; pick a stay near the parade and street party, and book early.
pride-weekend-hotels.body_html:
Blackpool Pride fills the town, and the guest houses go first. If you want a hotel near the action, decide on your base early. Below are the stays closest to the Lord Street street party and the walk to the Promenade parade.

When is Blackpool Pride?

The 20th anniversary Pride ran from 5 to 7 June 2026, with the parade on Saturday 6 June at 11am along the Promenade between Burlington Road West and Springfield Road. It also included a free two-day Rainbow Quarter street party along Lord Street, run by more than 20 local businesses. Dates for Pride 2027 have not been announced; check our Pride page and the official Blackpool Pride site for updates. Our seasonal notes describe Pride as usually early June.

Which stays are best for Pride?

  • Pride Lodge: one minute from the station and 2 minutes from Mardi Gras; its own tips say to book early for Pride and Illuminations weekends.
  • Mardi Gras and Q Accommodation: right on Lord Street, where the street party runs.
  • Trades Hotel and Bar and Welhorny's: men-only, 1 minute from Mardi Gras.
  • Rendezvous Bar and Rooms: at the station end of Lord Street, 2 minutes from Mardi Gras.
  • Peek-a-Booze and Lu-Lu's Cabaret Lounge: lively budget rooms on Dickson Road, 2 to 3 minutes from Mardi Gras.

How early should I book?

Rooms sell out early for Pride, often with three-night minimums according to our season notes. Book as soon as dates are released, and keep a flexible-cancellation option if the property offers it.

How do I get to the parade from my hotel?

The parade runs along the Promenade, a longer walk than the quarter itself: the North Pier is 6 to 10 minutes from most stays and the Tower 11 to 17. Trams run to Blackpool North from the Promenade; check our travel guide and Blackpool Transport for event-day arrangements.

What about the weekend nightlife?

  • Book Funny Girls early; Friday and Saturday sell out first.
  • The Flying Handbag and Mardi Gras are the main late-night anchors.
  • Check what's on for any Pride-linked events.

Can I bring a group?

Some guest houses do not take group bookings; see group planning. The Rainbow Quarter reference site has more on past Prides.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

illuminations-breaks.title: Illuminations Breaks: Gay Friendly Stays Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
illuminations-breaks.description: Plan an Illuminations break in Blackpool with a gay friendly hotel: 2026 season dates, stays within walking distance of the lights and autumn show nights.
illuminations-breaks.h1: Gay-friendly stays for the Blackpool Illuminations
illuminations-breaks.intro: The lights run into early November, so autumn is a lovely time for a Blackpool break; here are the stays to pick and the dates.
illuminations-breaks.body_html:
The Blackpool Illuminations turn the seafront into a long, glowing night out, and autumn weekends in a gay guest house are a classic. They are busy, so book early.

When are the Illuminations?

The lights usually run from early September to early November. In 2026 they were switched on on 4 September, with the full display running to 1 November, followed by a shorter stretch with Christmas by the Sea until 3 January 2027. Dates for later years are not in our data, so check the official Blackpool listings.

Which stays suit an Illuminations break?

  • Pride Lodge: its own tips say to book early for Pride and Illuminations weekends. About 9 minutes to North Pier.
  • Lawrence House: the closest in our list to the pier, about 6 minutes, with a roof terrace and evening meals listed.
  • Lu-Lu's Cabaret Lounge and Peek-a-Booze: 7 to 8 minutes to the pier, with rooms above cabaret bars.
  • Chaps Hotel: 8 minutes to the pier, with themed rooms and a bar.
  • Westfield House and De-Lovely Hotel: Lord Street guest houses, about 10 minutes from the pier.

How do I see the lights from my hotel?

North Pier is 6 to 11 minutes on foot from the listed stays and the Tower 11 to 17. The Promenade tram line carries you along the front. Trams run up Talbot Road to Blackpool North; confirm times with Blackpool Transport.

What is on in the evening?

  • Funny Girls ran its Halloween drag spectacular Wednesday to Sunday until 1 November 2026.
  • McGraths hosts a Halloween drag takeover on 31 October 2026, 8pm to 11pm.
  • Garlands has free drag daily from mid-afternoon.

Do rooms cost less than at Pride?

Our season notes call September and October the point for lights at lower prices, but weekends are still busy. Midweek in October is a calmer way to see the display: see quiet midweek breaks.

For a ready-made itinerary, use the 48-hour plan and swap the afternoon for a ride along the lights.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

quiet-midweek-breaks.title: Quiet Midweek Gay Breaks in Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
quiet-midweek-breaks.description: A midweek gay break in Blackpool: calm guest houses, and what is on Monday to Wednesday, from quizzes and bingo to free drag at Garlands.
quiet-midweek-breaks.h1: Quiet midweek breaks in gay Blackpool
quiet-midweek-breaks.intro: Monday to Wednesday is gentler and cheaper, with quizzes, bingo, karaoke and daily drag; here is where to stay and what to do.
quiet-midweek-breaks.body_html:
If your idea of a Blackpool break is a slow breakfast, a seafront stroll and an easy evening, midweek is perfect. Our season notes call spring the time for a gentler pace, and winter the cheapest time to stay. The scene does not stop, it just breathes.

Where should I stay for a quiet midweek break?

  • Westfield House: small, adults-only, listed as quiet.
  • Lawrence House: four-star, on a quiet street, and evening meals are a good option on a quiet midweek night.
  • De-Lovely Hotel: a breakfast and cocktail bar, open to non-residents with hours that vary by season.
  • Chaps Hotel: a bar and weekly offer if you stay a week.
  • The Prince Albert Hotel: men-only and discreet, with a lounge bar open through the day and evening.

What is on Monday to Wednesday?

DayWhat
MondayThe Flying Handbag Monday Mayhem from 8pm until 3am, karaoke; bingo and Blankety Blank with host Wayne at Peek-a-Booze from 7pm; inclusive LGBTQ+ football 7pm to 8pm
TuesdayKaraoke from 9pm at Peek-a-Booze with DJ Keiron
WednesdayQuizMania with Miss Amber 4pm to 8pm at The Flying Handbag, then karaoke; free bingo from 7pm at Peek-a-Booze; Funny Girls show night

Garlands also lists free drag every day from mid-afternoon. Funny Girls lists show nights Wednesday to Sunday, so Wednesday is the earliest midweek chance. Rendezvous is closed Monday and Tuesday on listed hours, so skip it then.

Is Blackpool dead on a Tuesday?

No, but it is quieter. Tuesday has fewer listed events, so combine karaoke with a seafront walk and an early dinner. Check venue pages before you set out, because smaller bars may trim hours in the quieter months.

Anything different on a Thursday?

Thursday brings Thirsty Thursday at The Flying Handbag, karaoke with Wayne at Peek-a-Booze, and the monthly LGBTQ+ swimming hour on the last Thursday of the month.

Staying a night longer? Link this with our food guide and the budget stays.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

first-time-gay-weekend-blackpool.title: First Gay Weekend in Blackpool: 48-Hour Plan | Blackpool.gay
first-time-gay-weekend-blackpool.description: A gay weekend in Blackpool for first-timers: where to stay, a Friday-to-Sunday plan, show booking tips and walking times around the Rainbow Quarter.
first-time-gay-weekend-blackpool.h1: Your first gay weekend in Blackpool, hour by hour
first-time-gay-weekend-blackpool.intro: A 48-hour plan for a first LGBTQ+ weekend in Blackpool: where to base yourself, what to book, and how to pace the nights.
first-time-gay-weekend-blackpool.body_html:
Blackpool rewards a plan, but not a rigid one. Everything in the Rainbow Quarter is a short walk, so your real decisions are where to sleep, what to book and how late you want to go. This plan keeps it simple.

Where should I stay on a first visit?

Pick a base within five minutes of the station. Pride Lodge (1 minute to the station), Mardi Gras (rooms above a community pub) and Q Accommodation (2 minutes) are the easiest starts. Browse the full stays list or stays near the station.

What does the weekend look like?

Friday

  • Arrive at Blackpool North and drop your bags.
  • Early drinks on Lord Street, then Garlands on Talbot Road: free entry, with resident queens on from mid-afternoon on listed times.
  • Late night at The Flying Handbag on Queen Street, with a Friday night hosted by Miss Amber.

Saturday

  • Slow breakfast, then the seafront: North Pier is roughly 9 minutes from Pride Lodge and the Tower about 12.
  • Early evening: dinner at Garbo's in the Funny Girls building, listed at £29.85 for three courses on show nights.
  • Show: Funny Girls, with doors at 7pm and the show at 8:30pm on listed times.
  • After: karaoke and live music at Oscars, then The Flying Handbag.

Sunday

  • Roast at The Flying Handbag (noon to 5pm), Mardi Gras or De-Lovely. Book ahead on busy weekends.
  • A final walk along the Promenade before your train.

Do I need to book Funny Girls?

Yes for Friday and Saturday, which sell out first. Standing starts from about £10 and seats are around £17 to £35 depending on the night. Phone the box office about access needs.

Is it safe and easy to get around?

The quarter is compact and welcoming; read our safety page and pre-book a licensed taxi on busy nights. For late-night routes see getting there and getting home.

How do I make it my own?

  • Swap in a pub lunch or food stop.
  • Come midweek for a gentler version: quiet midweek breaks.
  • Check what is open tonight on the day.

getting-there-and-getting-home.title: Getting to Blackpool Gay Bars: Trains & Trams | Blackpool.gay
getting-there-and-getting-home.description: How to reach Blackpool's gay bars and hotels by train, tram or car, plus how to get back to your hotel late at night. Pointers to National Rail and Blackpool Transport.
getting-there-and-getting-home.h1: Trains, trams and getting back to your hotel late
getting-there-and-getting-home.intro: Blackpool North station is minutes from the gay bars; here is how to arrive, move around and get home safely after a late night.
getting-there-and-getting-home.body_html:
The Rainbow Quarter is easy to reach without a car. Blackpool North station is on its edge and most bars and stays are within a short walk. We do not publish timetables here because they change, so use the right sources for times.

How do I get to Blackpool by train?

Blackpool North is the main station. Our travel notes list direct trains from Manchester, Manchester Airport, York and Leeds, with a change at Preston from London. Check times and engineering works on National Rail before you travel.

From the stationWalk
Pride Lodge1 minute
Q Accommodation2 minutes
Mardi Gras3 minutes
Funny Girlsabout 2 minutes (see venue)
North Pierabout 9 minutes from Pride Lodge
Blackpool Towerabout 12 minutes from Pride Lodge

What about trams?

Trams run up Talbot Road to a Blackpool North stop by the station, so you can ride from the Promenade line to the quarter. All modern trams are step-free, while heritage trams have steps. For service patterns and last departures, check Blackpool Transport; do not rely on our notes for late services.

Can I drive and park?

The M55 runs almost to the seafront. Open-air car parks on Banks Street and Dickson Road are about three minutes from the bars, and Talbot Road multi-storey is around four minutes away. A full day costs roughly £13 to £19, with multi-day tickets cheaper per day. Some guest houses sell discounted passes, which you must buy before you park. Pride Lodge sells a pass at reception, Westfield House offers vouchers and Lawrence House has no on-site parking.

How do I get home late?

If you are staying in the quarter, you can usually walk: nearly every stay is within 8 minutes of the main bars. Otherwise taxis wait outside Funny Girls and at the station, and a pre-booked licensed taxi is wise on busy weekends. Travel in a group where you can, and keep your hotel's address and phone number handy; read our safety page as well.

Which stays make late nights easiest?

  • Mardi Gras, Trades Hotel and Bar and Peek-a-Booze: rooms in or above the bar.
  • Rendezvous Bar and Rooms: 1 minute to Queen Street.
  • See hotels with a bar.

What if I have access needs?

Heritage trams have steps; stays often have stairs. Phone ahead, and check individual stay pages.

drag-night-out.title: Drag Night Out in Blackpool: Funny Girls & More | Blackpool.gay
drag-night-out.description: Plan a drag night out in Blackpool: Funny Girls tickets and dinner, free drag at Garlands, Peek-a-Booze nights and booking tips for groups.
drag-night-out.h1: How to plan a drag night out in Blackpool
drag-night-out.intro: Blackpool has big-theatre drag, free pub drag and cabaret bars; here is how to pick, book and combine them in one night.
drag-night-out.body_html:
Drag shows in Blackpool come in three flavours: a full theatre production, free drag in a camp pub, and cabaret bars where the host is your friend by the end of the night. You can do all three in an evening.

What are my drag options?

  • Funny Girls (5 Dickson Road): drag cabaret show nights Wednesday to Sunday, with doors at 7pm and the show about 8:30pm to 11:30pm on listed times. Standing from about £10; seats about £17 to £35.
  • Garlands (Talbot Road): free entry and resident queens daily from mid-afternoon.
  • The Flying Handbag: drag hosts including Miss Amber across Thursday and Friday nights, plus Monday Mayhem and QuizMania.
  • Peek-a-Booze, McGraths Bar and Hotel and Lu-Lu's Cabaret Lounge: cabaret bars that also have rooms.

Do you need to book Funny Girls?

Yes for Fridays and Saturdays, which sell out first. Box office hours are listed as Monday to Friday, 9:30am to 5:30pm. Some shows use pyrotechnics and loud bangs, and the venue asks you to phone about access.

Can I have dinner first?

Garbo's pre-show dinner in the Art Deco restaurant runs on show nights, listed at £29.85 for three courses. See our food guide.

What is a good drag evening in order?

  1. Afternoon or early evening: free drag at Garlands.
  2. Dinner at Garbo's, or another venue with food.
  3. Doors at Funny Girls at 7pm.
  4. Aftershow karaoke at Oscars, in the same building, from around 11pm Wednesday to Saturday.
  5. Finish at The Flying Handbag.

What about special seasons?

Funny Girls runs seasonal shows: the Halloween show until 1 November 2026, a New Year's Eve party, and 2027 shows including Spring Fling and Heatwave. Viva Blackpool lists drag brunches on 17 April, 11 September and 18 December 2027, from £39.95. McGraths has a Halloween takeover on 31 October 2026.

Tips for groups

  • Decorating your table or bringing a cake is welcomed at Funny Girls.
  • All venues are LGBTQ+ spaces first, and most are 18+, so bring ID.
  • See group planning and what's on.

Full performer profiles live on the Rainbow Quarter reference site.

hen-and-birthday-groups.title: Hen & Birthday Groups: Gay Blackpool Stays | Blackpool.gay
hen-and-birthday-groups.description: Hen, stag and birthday groups in gay Blackpool: which stays and shows welcome groups, which do not, and how to book respectfully for a big party.
hen-and-birthday-groups.h1: Hen, stag and birthday groups in gay Blackpool
hen-and-birthday-groups.intro: Blackpool is a great celebration town, but the quarter has house rules; here is which stays and shows suit groups and which do not.
hen-and-birthday-groups.body_html:
Birthday parties and hen dos are a Blackpool tradition, and the gay bars are happy to see a good-natured group. They are also LGBTQ+ spaces first, so the best groups arrive respectful and booked ahead.

Which shows welcome groups?

  • Funny Girls: you are welcome to decorate your table or bring a cake. Book well ahead for Fridays and Saturdays, and ask about dinner and show bundles.
  • The Flying Handbag: takes booth bookings for birthdays and parties, and can add a cold buffet if you book about two weeks ahead.
  • Viva Blackpool: lists drag and bottomless brunches through the year; see what's on.

Which stays suit a group?

Bars with rooms are the natural fit if you want to stay where the party is: Mardi Gras, Peek-a-Booze and Lu-Lu's Cabaret Lounge (about 26 en-suite rooms). Walking times from Lu-Lu's: 4 minutes to Funny Girls, 5 to The Flying Handbag.

Which stays do not take stag or hen bookings?

Westfield House is listed as not taking stag or hen bookings. Always ask before booking a block of rooms, particularly at the quieter guest houses such as Lawrence House. Another guest house, The Gynway, also does not accept them, according to our notes.

What are the house rules?

  • Men-only places stay men-only, including Trades Hotel and Bar, The Prince Albert Hotel, Welhorny's and the Growlr Club upstairs at Man Bar. Do not book a mixed group there.
  • Many stays are adults-only, and most venues are 18+, so bring ID.
  • Be kind to regulars and performers.

How do I plan a group night?

  1. Pick your show night first; see drag night out.
  2. Book the stay, then the dinner; see food guide.
  3. Agree a late-night meeting point and a way home; see getting home.

Can we choose a quieter date?

Yes: midweek is easier for large tables and cheaper rooms; see quiet midweek breaks.

Policies, prices and facilities can change, so confirm details with the property before you book.

eat-before-a-night-out.title: Where to Eat Before a Night Out in Gay Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
eat-before-a-night-out.description: Where to eat before a night out in gay Blackpool: pre-show dinner at Funny Girls, Sunday roasts, bar food and bistros, all within a few minutes' walk of the bars.
eat-before-a-night-out.h1: Where to eat before a night out in the Rainbow Quarter
eat-before-a-night-out.intro: From a three-course dinner before the show to Sunday roasts and daytime bar food, here is where to eat in the quarter.
eat-before-a-night-out.body_html:
A good night out in Blackpool starts with food. These are the venues in our data that serve it, with the times listed so you can build an evening around them.

Where can I have dinner before a drag show?

Garbo's, the Art Deco restaurant at Funny Girls, serves a three-course pre-show dinner on show nights, 6pm to 8pm, at £29.85 a head on the listed price. Doors are at 7pm, so book the table when you book the show.

What other venues serve food?

  • The Flying Handbag: all-day food and Sunday lunch from noon to 5pm, with a sun terrace.
  • Mardi Gras: hot food and Sunday roasts; book ahead on busy weekends.
  • Peek-a-Booze: food daily 9am to 7pm on listed hours.
  • De-Lovely Hotel: Sunday roasts and a breakfast guests praise; its cocktail bar is open to non-residents.
  • Antinous Lounge & Bistro (42 Banks Street): a lounge and bistro off Lord Street, a couple of minutes from North Pier.
  • The Blackpool North: a public bar and grill open from midday until late.
  • Lawrence House: evening meals listed, handy on a quiet night.

Where is best for a Sunday roast?

Several Rainbow Quarter venues serve roasts every Sunday, among them The Flying Handbag, Mardi Gras and De-Lovely. Reserve ahead; see what's on.

What is a sensible food-then-show timeline?

  1. Early evening: check in and freshen up.
  2. 6pm: dinner at Garbo's, or another venue.
  3. 7pm: doors at Funny Girls.
  4. 11pm: aftershow at Oscars.

Any tips for dietary needs?

We have no dietary details in our data, so phone ahead for allergies and special diets, and ask about cash-only bars such as Lu-Lu's.

Planning a longer trip? Use the 48-hour plan or compare stays above the bar.
